_meta.purpose: Raw read-only AWS state supporting the SPIKE findings on ignore_changes=[task_definition] drift. Preserved so the spike can be revised without re-querying AWS.
commands_run: aws ecs describe-services --cluster beta-001-cluster --services beta-001-web-service beta-001-worker-system-service beta-001-worker-user-service --region us-east-1 --query 'services[].{name:serviceName,taskDefinition:taskDefinition,controller:deploymentController.type,desired:desiredCount,running:runningCount}'
aws ecs list-task-definitions --family-prefix beta-001-worker-system --status ACTIVE --sort DESC --max-items 3 --region us-east-1
_meta.note_on_state: Collected AFTER the incident was resolved by a full app deploy on all four stacks. Running revision == latest revision at collection time, so this dump shows the CONVERGED state, not the divergence itself. It is evidence for WHICH RESOURCES a live revision references (Q4) and for the deployment-controller split (Q1), not for the drift being present today.

_finding_controller_split: Only the web service uses CODE_DEPLOY. Both worker services use the plain ECS deployment controller. The ecs_service module applies ignore_changes=[task_definition] UNCONDITIONALLY to every service, while its inline comment justifies it with 'CodeDeploy gerencia a task definition durante deployments' (modules/ecs_service/main.tf:155). The justification names a mechanism that applies to web only.

_finding_referenced_resource_classes.note: This is the Q4 enumeration, read off a real live revision.
_finding_referenced_resource_classes.ssm_parameters: 16 secrets, each a distinct SSM parameter ARN. This is the class that fired in the incident. DD_API_KEY is ABSENT (destroyed by terraform #711 and the revision re-registered clean); DATA_DOG_API_KEY is PRESENT and is a different, live variable.
_finding_referenced_resource_classes.execution_role: arn:aws:iam::405749097490:role/ecsTaskExecutionRole — referenced by ARN. NOT declared as an aws_iam_role resource anywhere in the terraform repo (grep found only hardcoded ARN string references and one aws_iam_role_policy attached to it). Terraform cannot destroy the role itself.
_finding_referenced_resource_classes.log_group: /ecs/beta-001-worker-system — IS terraform-managed (aws_cloudwatch_log_group.this in modules/ecs_service/main.tf:1-10). awslogs-create-group is NOT set, so the group must pre-exist.
_finding_referenced_resource_classes.volumes: empty on this task definition; the module supports them (modules/ecs_service/main.tf:56-62).

_not_researched: Whether any noncurrent/aged ACTIVE revision on any family still references /<stack>/DD_API_KEY (only the current running revision was checked, per family, on one stack).

The atento-001, demo-001 and shared-001 clusters were NOT dumped — only beta-001. The four stacks are assumed structurally identical because they share the ecs_service module, but this was not verified per-stack.
